evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390: Next and Back, the clickable step list, ArrowLeft/Right on the case file (Step 1 to 2 by keyboard), Back disabled on step 1, the status flips Open to Closed on step 5, and Next becomes 'Start over' and resets to step 1 with the panel at the top. evidence.first_screen: 1440x900 and 390x844 both show the specific promise and both actions, but nothing in view backs it up. At 1440 the sample heading sits at the very bottom and the right half is empty. At 390 the viewport ends at the sample heading with no case file in sight.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Alert reviews an examiner can follow without you in the room.' plus the lede 'Casefold is a case-file tool for BSA officers at community banks and credit unions. evidence.fit: The examiner lead is carried through an 'examiner asks / in the record / in the sample case' table that points back to specific steps. The board gets a dated 'Board brief' document (what it is, what it is not, who writes in a record, security status 'There is no SOC 2 report yet', cost, what the sandbox involves) written to be taken into the meeting. All sandbox actions are mailto:sandbox@casefold.example with the manual setup stated, and the dark close lists the three steps after you email.
evidence.distinctiveness: The page is built from the product: the hero is a split with a live case file (status chip, Owner and Next action, mono timestamps), the record section is a table of examiner questions mapped to the sample, and the board section is styled as a brief document. The Charter display, Helvetica text and mono-for-data system suits a compliance record. The three-box flow and dark CTA band are familiar parts.
evidence.proof: At 1440 the case file is in the first viewport and operable. Step 1 shows four deposits $9,400/$9,650/$9,200/$9,800 totalling $38,050 (checked), and later steps stay consistent ($3,900/week history, earlier alert ALT-1764 cited in the reason). It is labelled 'Fictional customer, staff and amounts. Illustrative only.' in its header at every width, and in the footer.
evidence.craft: There is a deliberate token scale (spacing --s-1..9, clamp type, colours), crisp hierarchy and passing contrast (axe clean at 390 and 1440). Minor defects: at 1440 the step tabs wrap 'What the examiner sees' onto three lines in a cramped 2px-gap strip. The folded-section 'Show' buttons are 28px tall. Because the hero copy is sticky, a tall blank column sits beside the case file once it grows.
evidence.mobile: 390: the hero is recomposed with stacked full-width-feeling buttons, and the case file starts at the bottom of the first screen with its fictional label. Tabs collapse to numbers at 62x44 and the pager to two 44px buttons. Menu opens and closes and closes on link tap (tapped 'For the board', landed at the section, menu closed) and on Escape. No overflow at 390 or 320. However: after tapping 'Next step' at 3 and 4, the newly added section appears below the fold and you have to scroll to see it (only the status chip and step note change near the tap). The 'Show' buttons are 28px. The header CTA is hidden under 480px.
evidence.honesty: The sample label is in the artifact header next to the data at 390. Before you click, the primary action says exactly what happens (one email, manual setup, login reply, sample alerts only). The no-compliance, no-regulator and no-SOC 2 points sit inside the board brief as plain status lines, without undermining confidence. Some product facts are invented beyond the brief: CSV import, 'sandbox itself has no charge', per-institution quotes.
evidence.interaction: Operated at 1440/768/390: tabs, Next step/Back, and the keyboard tablist (End jumped to step 5 with focus moved; Home and arrows wired). On each step the status changes Open, Assigned, In review, Awaiting approval, Decided, and the Owner/Next action update. Earlier parts fold to one-line summaries with Show/Hide toggles. Step 5 moves History to the top. Back and Last step are disabled at the ends. No console errors. There is no 'start over' at the end (Back or tab 1 only), and the Show controls are small.
evidence.copy: Customer-world nouns throughout: 'Refer for a SAR decision', 'I am not satisfied this is ordinary business', 'It starts after your monitoring system raises the alert, and stops before the SAR is filed', 'We say so up front rather than after procurement'. Buttons say what happens. A few section headings run long (the board H2 is four lines at 1440), and 'Last step' as a disabled label is a default-feeling choice.
evidence.first_screen: 1440x900: the promise, the lede naming the audience, the action with its consequence spelled out, and the operable, labelled sample case are all in one viewport. 390x844: promise, action and the 'what happens' note are in view, but only the sample's title, label and step numbers peek at the bottom, so the backing evidence is not yet in the phone's first screen.

problems: 390: after 'Next step' the newly revealed case-file section lands below the fold, so the main feedback is out of view.
Small and cramped controls: 'Show' toggles are 28px tall, and at 1440 the step tab labels wrap to three lines in a tight strip.
It adds product and commercial facts the brief does not supply (CSV import, free sandbox, per-institution quotes).

reason: B puts a labelled, operable, internally consistent case file beside the promise in the first desktop screen. Its record table and board brief come from the product and the brief's two audiences, and its execution (type system, state changes on status/owner/next action, working mobile menu) is tighter. A has excellent copy and better mobile step feedback, but a desktop hero with an empty half, no proof in view, and a stock section structure. I would change my mind only if B's below-the-fold step feedback on phones proved to be the main way buyers meet the page and A's sticky-footer stepper clearly outperformed it there.
